Existing problem, not tracked by any finding: completeTitrationPlan copies the titration schedules onto maintenance under new schedule ids. A dose logged today against the titration slot therefore no longer matches, and today's maintenance slot shows as pending, which invites a second take that decrements stock again. Editing a schedule in place keeps its id, so past days rendered from live schedules show the new dose or time unless the DoseLog snapshot fields are used for history. That is the trade-off the finding itself suggests.

phaseLiveOn treats 'cancelled' phases as not live. A titration that ran and was then cancelled has endDate set to the cancel time. On its days, the still-active maintenance schedule shows as missed, and the titration's taken doses show only through the fallback. Counting cancelled phases as live is unsafe: a plan cancelled while still pending also gets endDate=now, with startDate set to its creation or recommended date, so it would falsely override maintenance history. Telling the two apart needs activation data.

activatePhase (phase-service.ts:145) and activateTitrationPlan reset startDate to now when they reactivate a phase. Missed slots from the phase's earlier active period then drop out of past-day history. Taken and skipped logs still show through the fallback.

The server's due window is 30 minutes and is clamped at local midnight, so a 23:4x slot can be missed if the dispatcher runs after 00:00. A slot added late the same day fires right away if it falls inside the window.

core-duplication#3 only normalises future pulls. Dexie rows already holding null optional fields from earlier pulls keep them until the row is pulled again. A non-destructive sweep (null to missing key) would need either a Dexie version or a one-time runtime pass, and the schema package owns versions.

The migration upload ignores accepted serverUpdatedAt. On a device whose clock is more than 60s ahead, the server clamps updatedAt but the local row keeps the higher value. Because a newer local updatedAt always wins on pull, another device's edit that lands inside that skew window is not applied on this device. The window is narrow and it is an edge case.

When the server keeps a newer version (LWW rejects the push but acks it), the local row stays stale and relies on the pull to fetch the newer row. If this device's cursor already passed that row, which needs a lagging device clock, the device stays divergent. The old stamping behaviour was also divergent.

A pull retry timer (scheduleFailedPullRetry) can still be set after stopEngine, because schedulePull checks only engineSuspended. It is harmless in practice: after a wipe the pull returns nothing, and a 401 stops the retries.

modeChosenByUser defaults to false for existing users who switched to local before this change, so auto-detect can still flip them if the server has data. After a switch-to-local the cloud is normally wiped, so this is unlikely.
